# Security Assessment Service for Code Generated by Open-Weight LLMs

Diploma project, Software Engineering, group SE-2408.

A web service that sends coding tasks to several open-weight LLMs, scans the generated code with
static security analysers, maps the findings to CWE, and reports which model produces more
insecure code and under which prompt conditions.

## Problem, users, outcomes

- **Problem.** LLMs regularly generate vulnerable code, and teams that run open-weight models
  locally have no ready tool to compare models by the security of their output.
- **Target users.** Development and DevSecOps teams choosing a model for internal use, security
  engineers, researchers and instructors.
- **Expected outcomes.** A working service with an API and a web UI; a per-model report
  (share of insecure outputs, CWE distribution, model ranking); a reproducible evaluation method.

Details: [docs/project-proposal.md](docs/project-proposal.md).

## Scope and status

Pre-defense 1 (24 October 2026): analysis and design are done, no running service yet.
The scope and non-goals are in the proposal. Early pipeline experiments live in the course
research project (pilot with Bandit on 15 Python tasks), summarised in
[docs/pilot-results.md](docs/pilot-results.md).

## Technologies (proposed)

Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, vLLM / Ollama, Bandit, Semgrep, CodeQL, Docker,
a web UI framework (open decision). Justification: [docs/technology-comparison.md](docs/technology-comparison.md).

## Setup, run, test

Requirements: Docker with Compose; [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for running tests locally.

```bash
cp .env.example .env        # then replace the passwords; change API_PORT if 8000 is busy
docker compose up --build --wait
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
```

### Model server

The generation worker calls any OpenAI-compatible API set by `LLM_BASE_URL` (vLLM, Ollama).
The default points to Ollama on the Docker host: it must listen on an address that containers can
reach (see `OLLAMA_HOST`), and the host firewall must allow it. Do not expose it to untrusted networks.

To run the pipeline without a model, use the stub that always returns the same vulnerable code:

```bash
docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.stub.yaml up --build --wait
```

### Evaluation run

Model names are passed to the model server as they are.

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/runs -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"models": ["<model>"], "task_set": "builtin-python-15", "conditions": ["baseline", "security_prefix"]}'
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/runs/1
```

| Endpoint | Returns |
|---|---|
| `GET /tasks` | The built-in 15 tasks of the pilot |
| `POST /runs` | Creates a run; optional `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `seed` |
| `GET /runs/{id}` | Status, progress, failed jobs, generated code and findings |

Interactive API documentation: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`.

Current limits: Bandit is the only analyser, `analyser_repair` is not implemented, and generated
code is only scanned, never executed. A job that hits a database or queue error is retried until it succeeds.

### Health and data

`/health` returns 200 when the database and the queue respond, otherwise 503 with the failed check.
The API listens on localhost only because it has no authentication yet.

Stop the stack with `docker compose down`; add `-v` to also delete the database and queue data.
The PostgreSQL password is applied only when its volume is first created.

Tests:

```bash
cd backend && uv run pytest
```

End-to-end test against a stack started with the stub (set the port from `.env`):

```bash
cd backend && E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8000 uv run pytest tests/test_e2e.py
```
